name: Fodder Radish (Oil/Tillage Radish)
harvestProduct: grazing/fodder (leaves and roots) and green manure/soil-loosening biomass, killed by frost or herbicide

evidence.quote: This species is both cold- and drought-resistant, but not tolerant of waterlogged conditions. Radishes grow best when planted early enough to allow six weeks of growth before regular frosts. Radishes are winter hardy plants and are tolerant of light frosts, but generally show injury when temperatures drop below the -0°C.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA (Truter, Dannhauser, Smith & Trytsman), 2019

evidence.quote: The normal planting date is January/February, however, in the cooler eastern Highveld regions, the crop can be planted as early as middle December.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: This crop is adapted to the cooler eastern parts of the country; where rainfall is reasonably reliable during January to April.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Radishes are only moderately cold-hardy and need about six weeks of favourable growing conditions to produce sufficient biomass to achieve most potential benefits (Gruver et al., 2014)
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Only a minimum growth period is sourced (about six weeks / 42 days); no maximum or exact day-count to full termination was found.

evidence.quote: When this crop is planted in rows, it is recommended that rows are planted 90 cm apart with plant interspacing of 35 cm – 50 cm from each other. However, when planted as a cover crop, denser seeding rates are used (usually broadcasted) and narrower rows of maximum 50 cm apart are preferred.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: rows are planted 90 cm apart with plant interspacing of 35 cm – 50 cm from each other
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: The seeding rate of 2 kg/ha in rows is advised and 4 kg/ha when sown in a broadcast fashion.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Production values of up to 6 tons/ha can be expected with a protein value of 18% – 21% for roots and 20% – 30% for leaves.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: It grows large very quickly and has a large nitrogen uptake of around 20kg/ha.
evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016 — this is N UPTAKE (scavenging), not fixation; radish is not a legume, so nFixedKgPerHa is left null.

evidence.quote: Tillage radish is killed by frost or herbicide before the start of the next growing season.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

varieties.name: Nooitgedacht
varieties.note: Most common fodder-radish cultivar in SA.

evidence.quote: The most common cultivar is Nooitgedacht, with alternative cultivars such as Samurai, Sakurajuma, Star 1650 and 1651 and a soft leaf cultivar by the name of Sterling.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 15: Radish, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

zoneNotes.highveld: Adapted to the cooler eastern parts of the country with reliable Jan-Apr rainfall; can be sown as early as mid-December on the eastern Highveld.
zoneNotes.western-cape: "More recently, alternative cultivars are being grown in the western parts of the country as well" — no specific months given for this region.

gaps: No exact upper day-count to termination; only a minimum of 'about six weeks' (~42 days) of favourable growth is sourced.
Western Cape (winter-rainfall) sow months are only vaguely referenced ('more recently grown in the western parts') without specific months, so winter pattern left empty.
Requires 650mm/year minimum rainfall per the source, which may not hold everywhere it's listed as grown — worth flagging for irrigated-only western-region use.
summary: Very well sourced from Grain SA's Part 15 (Radish): sow window (Jan/Feb, mid-Dec on Highveld), row/in-row spacing (90cm/35-50cm rows, narrower up to 50cm as cover crop), seed rate (2kg/ha rows, 4kg/ha broadcast) and fodder yield (up to 6 t/ha). Missing an exact days-to-termination number (only a 'six weeks minimum' growth requirement) and sow depth, so it stays at 'partial'.
